hook: If you've ever left a conversation feeling uneasy and then spent three hours talking yourself out of it
topic: Trusting your instincts — the signal that arrived before the framework
body:
**If you've ever left a conversation feeling uneasy and then spent the next three hours convincing yourself you were overthinking — your instincts were not the problem.**

What was happening in that moment is that your nervous system picked something up before your conscious mind had language for it. A small inconsistency. A warmth that felt bright but somehow not quite directed at you. A story told in a way that didn't quite track.

You felt it. And then, because you had no framework to stand behind it, you did what kind, reasonable people do — you extended the benefit of the doubt. You filed it away.

And then, three months later, you found out you were right.

The signal was real. It was always real. You just weren't given the tools to trust it.

Your gut isn't noise. It's pattern recognition your brain finished before you consciously caught up. The work isn't learning to feel more — it's learning to stop talking yourself out of what you already know.

Next time you leave a conversation with that low hum of something being off — write it down before you rationalise it away. Just one sentence. You're training yourself to receive the signal, not dismiss it.

I go much deeper on this in the link in my bio — it's the whole framework for reading people more clearly.
